## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0a40d3a15c065fdefb31103dd8893c71d7b1b583`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md + docs/qa/scenarios/README.md, docs/qa/scenarios/builds/travel_expense.json, docs/qa/scenarios/builds/travel_expense.provenance.json
Security-touching: no

PR #35222 (draft, `Refs #34920 (item: travel_expense fixture)`), rules face: the one governed path is the `scenario-eval` skill. Read for this record: card #34920 with every comment (claim 6984134425, dev report 6985513722), the ruling it carries (comment 6953792719 on #34687, the maintainer verbatim: 「两件都同意：构建提交进仓库，#34894 选 A」, recorded as "the verified builds the ask rounds run on are committed into the repository as fixtures beside their cards. Records, recordings and logs stay out of the tree as before"), the PR's file list and its net diff against `main` at this head, the head's check-runs, and the cited code on `main` (merge-base ec227fc7; the diff touches no file under packages/, scripts/ or turbo.json). The second half of the ruling (#34894, option A) is a different decision and has no text in this diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Governed rule text (the hits file): right.** Three hunks. §1 says where the ask round's `F` lives (`docs/qa/scenarios/builds/ID.json`, pointing at the README's Verified builds section) and adds 「只经 PR」 to the existing "a changed build is named in Reading" rule. §4 turns the ask-round example into a runnable command on the committed travel_expense fixture, absolute path through `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. §5 adds the one sentence the card asked for: 「轮所装的已验证构建不是运行产物而是 fixture,在树里(`docs/qa/scenarios/builds/`),只随 PR 改,⛔ 轮不写它」. Each is the ruling's consequence; none changes what a round measures, how it is configured, how it is recorded or where findings go.
- **Loader accept-set: unchanged, right.** `loadScenarios` reads the card directory non-recursively and keeps names ending `.json` (packages/qa/scenarios/src/loader.ts:168-171). The entry `builds` is a directory name without that suffix, so neither the fixture nor its provenance is ever offered to the card schema. The runner's default card directory goes through the same function (packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts:394), as do the library tests.
- **Published surface: unchanged, right.** `pack-library.mjs` copies two directories one level deep, regular `.json` files only (packages/qa/scenarios/scripts/pack-library.mjs:11-12, :28, :37-38): `builds` is skipped on both conditions (no `.json` suffix, not a regular file), and README.md was never copied. The package's `files` are dist, README.md and CHANGELOG.md (packages/qa/scenarios/package.json:105-109). The packed-tarball test uses the same one-level filter and goes red on any other JSON in the tarball (packages/qa/scenarios/test/build/packed-tarball.test.ts:55, :122-125). The build's turbo inputs are `docs/qa/scenarios/*.json`, one level (turbo.json:721, packages/qa/scenarios/turbo.json:8), so a fixture change does not rebuild the package.
- **So the README sentence "The loader and the packed library read this directory one level deep, so `builds/` is neither a card nor shipped" is true in code**, at the lines above.
- **Runner contract the skill and the README lean on: right, no runner change needed.** `--template F` is read with `readFileSync` and never written (cli.ts:469-470). The record's top-level `template` is the file's basename and sha256 (packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/summary.ts:70-72, cli.ts:365-371 and :472). Ask mode installs the supplied build with no authoring turn, no score and no iterate (packages/qa/scenarios/README.md:313 and :315-322). A template whose namespace is not the card's is skipped (packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts:2021-2024), which is why the skill keeps one command per card.
- **Fixture integrity, read off the head's blobs** (`git show` piped to sha256sum and to a JSON parse; nothing built, run or re-run): `builds/travel_expense.json` hashes to 5fe6f452d36fe56a0ecf0f8c782394076953baeb99ef2499763991e119a29989, equal to the provenance file's `sha256`. It is 93,382 bytes, 3,182 lines with no newline at the end of the file, so it was not reformatted on the way in, and it parses as JSON. Its manifest namespace `demotravel` is `demo` plus the card's code `travel`, and its three datasets (claim_lines, reimbursement, trip_plan) carry the measures the card's `expect.datasets` declares. The provenance file parses as JSON; its `cardSha256` 9d0c7dad107579b8e77d0c7924ec8c44ebf0bb446d3f3f0a526c32828eca262a equals the sha256 of `docs/qa/scenarios/travel_expense.json` at this head and on `main`; its `runner` ec227fc7 is the merge-base. `builds/` holds exactly these two files.
- **Not measured by this review:** that these bytes are the scratch run's verified pre-iterate build (the run record is outside the tree; the dev report gives the re-score evidence), and the fresh-container ask run on the committed file (dev report). No check-run exercises either.
- **Check-runs on this head:** every run completed, each success or skipped. Test Core, every Lint leg, every Type Check leg, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards and Check PR Size read success; Check Changeset is skipped under the `skip-changeset` label.
- **The security line reads no.** No changed hunk of the skill or the README teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The fixture is an app build the runner installs as data: it carries the demo app's three permission sets, their row-level rules and one ask-surface skill as build content, which is what the round measures and not instruction to any fleet agent. The provenance `login: oauth_token` is the login kind, not a secret. A targeted scan of the fixture (not a line-by-line read) found no key, token, password, URL, e-mail address or absolute path, and no network, process, eval or require call in its hook and action sources. The line is inert on this PR: `.claude/**` is the claude-tree row, Tier S with no low-risk arm (scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs:1376), and the paths-filled template prints no such line. If the seat reads "teaches" as covering security configuration carried inside a fixture, this line is the one value to change; nothing lands on it either way (see ③).

### ② Semver level

- Nothing published changes: no file under packages/, no schema, no shipped JSON (① shows `builds/` and the README never reach the tarball). The `skip-changeset` label is right, and the body's `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6985513722, `open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: none; agreed, see ①.
- Deviation 1 (worked on the card-thread branch, no extra worktree): process only, no effect on the diff.
- Deviation 2 (provenance names the requested alias `opus` and effort `high`, not the served model id): accepted deviation, N5 below.
- Deviation 3 (signed trailer in the PR body): prose, nothing to judge.
- Deviation 4 (no reviewer request sent): right to leave with the seat. Landing: the PR is 3,232 changed lines (3,226 added, 6 removed), over the 3,000-line threshold of the AGENTS.md merge rule (c), so it lands the Tier H way, on an authorized APPROVED review and then the owning seat, or by the maintainer's merge or enqueue, whatever this record says. It is a draft with no auto-merge armed, as it must be.
- Partial landing: the body's `Refs #34920 (item: travel_expense fixture)` is a non-closing keyword, and the claim (6984134425) named this route beforehand. The card stays open for order_to_cash; its Done-when (both dataset cards, no build step) is met for one of the two at this head.
- Out-of-scope findings in the report: the order_to_cash seed refusals go to #34986 (open). The roll-up charge goes to "the epic filer"; I found no open card that carries it. For the seat to confirm a carrier; the skill's §4 note names #34986 alone (N3).
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside author to name.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no code; nothing to check.

### ④ Design judgment

**`.claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md` (hits)**, judged against the ruling, the card's Scope bullets, the rest of the skill, `lanes/eval.md` and the runner on `main`. The skill is internal (`metadata.internal: true`), so no eval prompt applies; the scenario it is accepted against is the card's Done-when.

- **Faithful to the ruling, no widening of substance.** "Committed … as fixtures beside their cards" is `docs/qa/scenarios/builds/`, inside the file surface the card allowed. "Records, recordings and logs stay out of the tree as before" is the unchanged §5 sentence, now followed by the distinction. The card's "changes only by a PR … a daily round never writes it" is 「只随 PR 改,⛔ 轮不写它」 and §1's 「换了构建(只经 PR)」. The card's "`--template` reads it from the tree; the record names its sha256" is §1 and §4 plus the §5 Environment rule that already existed (build file name and sha256 from the record's `template`).
- **No contradiction inside the skill.** §0's 「卡、runner、评分器都在本仓」 now holds for the build as well. §0's runner pin covers the fixture, which sits in the same checkout and so moves only between rounds; when it moves, the record's sha256 shows it and §1 has Reading name it. The Guardrails line 「⛔ 不开 PR … 立卡交车道」 composes with the new sentence: the seat neither writes nor PRs the fixture, so a refresh is a card to the lane.
- **No contradiction with `lanes/eval.md`.** ⑤ (ask mode on the dataset cards, local app, subscription login, no cloud repository) and the boundary (no `os-dev`, no product code, no PR) stand as they were; the charter needs no line for this.
- **Tried to break it.** Can a round write `F`? No: the runner only reads it, `--out` is elsewhere and the install goes into a blank host of its own. Does the §4 example work from the package directory? Yes: the shell expands the substitution in the caller's working directory before pnpm changes directory, and the path is absolute, which the runner README asks for (packages/qa/scenarios/README.md:248, :599). Does the §1 grep for dataset cards or control cards pick up a fixture? No: both globs are one level. What happens for order_to_cash, whose fixture does not exist? A command on the missing path stops at cli.ts:469 before any card runs, and the §4 note says only travel_expense is runnable until the file is committed.

**`docs/qa/scenarios/README.md`, the Layout lines and the Verified builds section (implementing).** Sentence by sentence: the purpose sentence matches `lanes/eval.md` ⑤; the provenance sentence matches the committed file field for field; "builds nothing; its record names the file's sha256" and "A round never writes it" match the runner lines in ①; "it changes only by a PR, when the card or the runner changes" is the card's own wording; the loader and packed-library sentence is true in code. Two imprecisions are N1 and N4.

**`docs/qa/scenarios/builds/travel_expense.json` and `travel_expense.provenance.json` (implementing).** They agree with what the skill and the README say about them, as far as the tree can show: see the integrity line in ①. The provenance records every item the card's Scope lists (sha256, runner sha, the model that built it) plus the card's sha256, the package source and the driver.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, none of which changes what a round does. All sit off the prose faces, so they are accepted deviations or follow-up cards, not fixes on this head:

- N1 (nit) — §1 gives `F` as `docs/qa/scenarios/builds/ID.json` for both cards it lists, and the README says "each dataset card's verified build is a fixture here" right after naming order_to_cash and travel_expense. At this head `builds/order_to_cash.json` does not exist, and the only disclosure is the bash comment in §4. No wrong action follows (the runner stops on the missing path, and the skill's general `not measured` rule covers the record). It closes by itself when the order_to_cash fixture lands under #34920; a clause in §1 would be the better place until then.
- N2 (nit) — §5 says 「轮所装的已验证构建」, broader than the ruling's "the verified builds the ask rounds run on". Read literally it also covers a `--modes scratch,ask` round, which installs that run's own scratch build (a run product), and an ad-hoc template-mode `F`. The seat can neither commit nor open a PR, so nothing follows from the wider reading; 「问数日轮所装的」 would match the ruling and the README.
- N3 (nit) — the §4 note 「order_to_cash 的构建等 #34986」 names one of the two blockers the PR's own evidence reports (the seed refusals; the other is the roll-up charge, Build 169/170). The operative condition is 「入库前」, the file's presence, so the pointer cannot mislead a round; #34920 is the card that actually carries the fixture.
- N4 (nit) — the README writes the flag as `--template docs/qa/scenarios/builds/ID.json`, a repository-relative path. Under `pnpm --filter` the runner resolves it against packages/qa/scenarios (cli.ts:469). The skill's example, which is what the seat runs, passes the absolute path.
- N5 (nit) — the provenance `author.model` is the requested alias. The card asks for "the model that built it", and the skill's own §2 standard is the served model, checked on the scorecard. The served id exists only in a run record in the card thread's container. Cheap now and impossible later: post the served id on the card thread while that record exists, and fold it into the provenance with the order_to_cash PR.
- N6 (nit) — nothing pins the fixture. No test compares `builds/ID.json` with its provenance `sha256`, or `cardSha256` with the card, so a card edit leaves a stale fixture green and the README's "when the card or the runner changes" has no detector. The place for it is packages/qa/scenarios, outside this card's fenced surface (held by #34780). Follow-up card for devx: a library test pinning the three (bytes to provenance, `cardSha256` to the card, namespace to the card), and a runner switch that writes out the verified pre-iterate build so the next fixture is not snapshotted by hand.
- N7 (nit) — the PR title is plural ("the dataset cards' verified builds") for one fixture and becomes the squash subject; the body's figures (3,229 lines, skill net +1) predate the second commit (3,232, net +2). Prose only.

Outside the diff, for whoever next edits these files: the §1 start-condition bullet is always met now (#34911 and #34882 both merged on 2026-11-17), and its rationale sentence describes the earlier project-files build of travel_expense, not the committed fixture; `docs/qa/scenarios/README.md` line 14 still calls the package "private, not published" while the new section speaks of its packed library. Neither is this PR's.

**VERDICT: PASS**
